svg.title: Levistack glossary
svg.desc: How to start (full route, one-shot, or a bare skill), the seven steps, the words around a run, nine groups, and all 66 skills plus 2 upstream skills. Modes inside output-savers and noslop are not separate catalog skills.
svg.text: How to start, what each group is, and what each skill does.
66 skills in 9 groups, plus 2 upstream skills.
task. A playbook matches, then all seven
Name a skill inside that command. It still
primes, hunts to confirm, proves, and
Type /skill alone. That skill runs by
itself. Prime, hunt, and deliver stay off.
Prime, hunt, and deliver always run on the full route and on a one-shot.
Route matches a playbook, or marks a named skill as a one-shot. Prime is output-savers reading your prompt. It does not rewrite your
words. Invoke restates the goal, then picks the first skill. Hunt is find-skills, and it runs every time. Apply runs the chain, one
skill at a time, at most four. Prove is fresh proof from verify. A push, MR, comment, install, or publish waits for your yes.
Deliver is polyglot-copywriter on prose for people, then output-savers as the last gate on the reply.
A named route for one kind of task: investigate, feature, bug-fix, refactor, design-shape, parallel,
prove-outside-diff, open-ended. It fills invoke and apply. The seven steps still run.
The skills for this task, at most four. Each one prepares, does the work, or verifies.
A push, MR, comment, install, or publish waits until you agree.
This host can start the skill by name.
The skill is a file on disk. Read its SKILL.md and follow it.
The only outside catalog find-skills may browse, and only after this catalog has no fit.
A skill in its own repo. The levistack plugin installs it. Edit it in that repo.
A folder of skills. It also ships as the plugin levistack-<group>.
The skills, agents, rules, commands, and hooks this repo publishes.
A helper for one bounded job. The session keeps the seven steps.
A standard that holds even when nobody invoked a skill.
A saved prompt you run as /name. /start runs use-levistack.
An opt-in check on a tool event. It runs only after you create ~/.levistack/<name>.on.
66 catalog skills, plus 2 upstream. concise, concise-light, concise-heavy, and principles live inside output-savers. noslop-code
lives inside noslop. Those are modes, not extra catalog skills.
Group order follows the path: front door, machinery, the work, the session, the catalog, then upstream.
The front door. Start a task, check the machine, or ask how.
Match a playbook, then run the seven steps. Start here.
Check the tools scripts call. Install nothing without a yes.
Say which skill fits and hand back a prompt. Do not start the work.
The machinery around a result: hunt, evidence, loops, lanes, handoff.
Search this catalog. On a miss, browse skills.sh, install, and run.
Frame a goal, run one evidence-led pass, or judge finished work.
Repeat one change until the named checks pass or a stop state hits.
Split, Contest, or Council. Then evidence judges the result.
Resume, catch up, recall, or write the note for the next session.
Design one auditable run when no narrower playbook fits.
Several lanes, one controller. Lanes do not merge or push.
One prompt on two or three models this host can spawn.
Name repeated friction and the strongest useful fix.
How code works, why it is shaped that way, and whether a plan holds.
Explain how the code works today. Read-only.
Explain why it is shaped this way, evidence on every step.
Grill a plan. Numbered questions, each with a recommended answer.
Answer from primary sources, or write questions for one person.
Read-only review that drives each open decision to a commitment.
Test first, prove the claim, keep behavior, and cut slop.
One failing test, the smallest pass, then refactor while green.
Fresh proof before any claim of done. Diagnose before editing.
Keep behavior the same while the structure changes.
Filter slop in handlers, UI, queries, config, tests, and comments.
The smallest change, named principles, and plain replies.
What a small diff can break outside itself, and why it is safe.
Audit dev caches. Delete only paths you approved.
Pick a shape, a stack, or a boundary, then build against it.
Settle types and module shape, compare two, then build one.
Detect, choose, build, evaluate, migrate, or document one.
Cache design for web and mobile, including offline.
Node.js services, APIs, middleware, and auth.
proto3, buf, gRPC or Connect, and schema breaks.
Compare stacks, cost a migration, or write a blueprint.
Spec, plan, review, and the writing that ships with the change.
A plan a stranger can follow: files, tasks, tests, and commits.
An execution-ready spec for a backend or API change.
An ADR, design doc, or RFC from the code and real alternatives.
Review a diff or MR. Watch stays until clean. Prep stops before merge.
Refresh, rework, or close a stale PR or MR, then code-review.
Split a messy tree into small commits with clean messages.
Draft the MR or PR description from the commits.
Slice a plan into end-to-end tickets, then draft them.
Docs and API handovers checked against the source.
A Bruno API collection, with auth and error examples.
Parse, create, or convert documents, images, and audio.
Changelog and release notes from the commits and the diff.
A blameless postmortem or near-miss, from evidence.
A recovery, deploy, or migration runbook with a rollback.
Color, screens, diagrams, explainers, prototypes, and polish.
Build a design system, then critique with it.
One screen or one component, including motion.
A technical diagram with an editable source and a checked export.
An evidence-based explainer, chart, timeline, or poster.
A throwaway prototype or wireframe for one design question.
Audit a shipped product: code, journeys, branding, motion.
Static canvas art, seeded generative art, or a short GIF.
The session itself. One next step, a later list, today's standup.
Shrink a stuck task to one next action and a 25-minute round.
Park a tangent in LATER.md and return to the task.
Today's standup from what you actually did.
Skills, agents, rules, commands, hooks, and whole setups.
Turn existing material into a skill, or merge skills.
Write a rule or coding standard.
Automate something on an agent event.
Write or refresh AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
Connect, diagnose, or build an MCP server.
Export or import an agent setup. Secrets are stripped.
Move an agent setup and a Mac in or out. Waits for a yes before writing.
Their own repos. The levistack plugin installs them. Edit them there.
Plain prose for people, in 97 languages, facts unchanged.
An SVG brand kit: icon, banner, static, and animated.
Each line is the index. The skill file owns the detail. 31 Oct 2026.
